lessons.title: literal comprehension: read → notice → explain → use
lessons.objective: Learner can understand, explain and use literal comprehension in speech or writing.
teach: Introduce literal comprehension through a short original example connected to everyday life.
Ask the learner what they notice before explaining the formal idea.
Model how to find evidence in the text or situation.
Guide the learner to answer using complete, meaningful language.
Remove prompts and ask for an independent response.

worked_example.prompt: Use an original mini-example to demonstrate literal comprehension.
worked_example.method: Notice the clue, explain what it means, connect it to the idea, and express the conclusion clearly.

lessons.checkpoint: Explain literal comprehension and create one original example.
lessons.mastery_signal: Accurate understanding + evidence/reasoning + clear independent expression.

interactive_activities.title: Read, notice, retell
interactive_activities.instructions: Use an original short passage or teacher-created example connected to 'Papa's Spectacles'. Identify a clue related to literal comprehension, then retell the important idea in your own words.

interactive_activities.title: Use the language
interactive_activities.instructions: Role-play a familiar situation in which new words: spectacles, pair, glanced, searching is useful. The learner must speak or write independently.

interactive_activities.title: Make your own example
interactive_activities.instructions: Create a short original example showing rhythm and simple rhyme. Explain why it demonstrates the concept.

misconception_remediation.trigger: thinking the spectacles were found in a new place rather than on Papa's head
misconception_remediation.diagnostic: Ask the learner to explain the idea and solve a near-example without hints.
repair: Identify the exact concept or prerequisite that is missing.
Return to one concrete, familiar example.
Think aloud and contrast the incorrect idea with the correct idea.
Ask the learner to explain the correction in their own words.
Reassess before moving to the next concept.
misconception_remediation.exit_criterion: Two consecutive accurate responses with an independent explanation.

critical_conditions: Learner can explain the key idea without copying.
Learner can solve or respond to an unfamiliar example.
mastery_policy.on_failure: Do not simply unlock the next chapter. Route the learner to the weakest concept/prerequisite, reteach, practise and reassess.
mastery_policy.on_mastery: Unlock spaced retrieval and cumulative review.

spaced_retrieval.rule: Use mixed retrieval; increase difficulty after correct independent recall; re-enter remediation after repeated failure.
